historical_references.context: Awbi ibn Abd al-Asad al-Lahmi was a prominent Arab chief who ruled over the Banu Hanifa tribe in the early Islamic period. He is said to have played a significant role in the Battle of Hunayn (633 AD) by leading a contingent of 2,000 men and supporting the Muslim army under the command of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). After the battle, Awbi is reported to have pledged allegiance to Islam and accepted the sovereignty of the Islamic state.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Baladhuri, Ansab al-Ashraf, vol. 3, p. 45 The name Awbi carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Awbi ibn al-Asad al-Thaqafi was a prominent Arab chieftain who ruled over the Banu Thaqif tribe in central Arabia. He is said to have played a crucial role in the military campaigns of the early Islamic conquests under the Umayyad Caliphs. Awbi is reported to have led the conquests of Kufa and Basra, and later Bahrain and Oman, in the 7th century. His military prowess and leadership skills earned him a reputed place in Islamic history.
